question.worked_solution:
Remember that the square root of a perfect square can be simplified using absolute value.

$$
\sqrt{{x}^{2}}=|x|
$$

Also, we notice that ${y}^{2}$ and ${z}^{2}$ are perfect squares.

First, we write the expression under the square root as a perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{{y}^{2}{z}^{2}} & =\sqrt{y\cdot y\cdot z\cdot z} \\  & =\sqrt{y\cdot z\cdot y\cdot z} \\  & =\sqrt{(yz)\cdot (yz)} \\  & =\sqrt{(yz)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we take the absolute value of the squared quantity:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{(yz)^{2}} & =|yz|\end{aligned}
$$
